title: Camel-Bean header injection allows bypass of header filtering
description: A header filtering bypass in the camel-bean component lets a crafted HTTP header change the bean method invoked by the route, so an attacker can reach methods that were never meant to be exposed.

title: Header injection through crafted HTTP query parameters
description: Query parameters supplied on an inbound HTTP request are promoted to Camel message headers without filtering, which allows an attacker to influence downstream route behaviour.

title: Deserialization of untrusted data in camel-sql
description: The SQL component deserializes data read from a database column without validating its type, so a poisoned row can lead to remote code execution when the exchange is processed.

title: Denial of service in HTTP/2 request handling
description: Malformed HTTP/2 priority frames are not released correctly, letting a remote client exhaust the connection pool of a Camel HTTP consumer.

title: Property access bypass in bean introspection
description: Bean introspection used by type converters can be tricked into invoking declared class loader methods, exposing internal state of the running integration.

title: Information disclosure through error responses in camel-jetty
description: Stack traces are returned to the caller when a route throws during unmarshalling, revealing internal endpoint URIs and credentials embedded in them.

title: XML external entity expansion in camel-xslt
description: The XSLT component resolves external entities by default when a stylesheet is loaded from an exchange body, which allows local file disclosure.

title: Server-side request forgery in camel-http via redirect following
description: The HTTP producer follows redirects to arbitrary hosts, so a route that fetches a caller supplied URL can be used to reach internal services.

title: Path traversal when writing attachments to disk
description: File names taken from multipart uploads are used unsanitised by the file producer, allowing writes outside the configured directory.

title: Unbounded memory allocation while decoding multipart requests
description: A multipart request without a length limit is buffered completely in memory, letting a remote caller drive the JVM into an out of memory condition.

title: HTTP/2 rapid reset denial of service
description: Rapid stream cancellation on an HTTP/2 connection consumes disproportionate server resources on Camel HTTP consumers built on the affected transport.

title: Command argument injection in camel-exec
description: Arguments passed to the exec component are concatenated into a shell command, so header values reaching the route can inject additional commands.

title: Buffer over-read in Snappy decompression used by camel-kafka
description: A corrupted Snappy frame makes the decompressor read past the end of the buffer and terminate the consumer thread.

title: Weak default TLS configuration in camel-mail
description: The mail component negotiates legacy TLS versions when no explicit SSL context is configured, allowing a downgrade by a network attacker.

title: Infinite loop when unpacking malformed archives in camel-zipfile
description: A truncated archive entry makes the zipfile data format loop indefinitely, pinning a CPU core for the lifetime of the route.

title: Schema parsing allows arbitrary class loading in camel-avro
description: Avro schemas read from an exchange can reference arbitrary classes, which are loaded eagerly during unmarshalling.
